DOCUMENT:
Vendor Comparison: Standard Parcel Delivery Contract
Larkspur Home, Operations, June 2026

1. Purpose
Our contract with our current standard-delivery carrier ends on 30 September 2026. This paper compares three shortlisted carriers and recommends which should carry our standard (two-to-four-day) parcels from October.

2. Volumes and requirements
We dispatch an average of 42,000 standard parcels a month: about 70% weigh under 2 kg (cushions, textiles, small homeware) and 30% weigh 2 to 10 kg (lamps, mirrors, small furniture). Our requirements are on-time delivery of at least 95%, a damage rate below 0.5%, full tracking, and a returns service.

Damage and loss matter to us commercially. Each damaged or lost parcel costs us on average £48 in replacement stock, return shipping and customer service time, and damaged items are the most common cause of one-star reviews.

3. Trial
Between 1 April and 31 May 2026, each shortlisted carrier delivered a share of our orders, allocated at random by the warehouse management system, about 5,000 parcels per carrier. We measured on-time delivery against the promised date, damage reported by customers within 14 days, and lost parcels.

Table 1. Prices and trial performance
Carrier | Price, under 2 kg | Price, 2-10 kg | On-time delivery | Damage rate | Lost per 10,000 parcels
SwiftDrop | £3.10 | £4.60 | 96.2% | 0.4% | 3
ParcelLine | £2.85 | £4.95 | 93.1% | 0.9% | 8
Meridian | £3.30 | £4.40 | 97.5% | 0.3% | 2

On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial, and all three offer full tracking and a returns service.

4. Cost comparison
Applying our 70/30 weight mix, the average cost per parcel is £3.55 for SwiftDrop, £3.48 for ParcelLine and £3.63 for Meridian. On 42,000 parcels a month, the monthly cost would be £149,100 for SwiftDrop, £146,160 for ParcelLine and £152,460 for Meridian. ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop and £6,300 a month against Meridian, or between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year.

5. Customer contact
"Where is my order?" contacts are our largest single category of customer service enquiry. During the trial, ParcelLine deliveries generated 6 such contacts per 1,000 parcels, compared with 11 for SwiftDrop and 10 for Meridian. ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts, and at an average handling cost of £3.20 per contact this would save about £670 a month at our volumes. From 1 May, ParcelLine parcels also carried our new proactive delivery-day text message, which we were testing on one carrier before rolling it out.

6. Other considerations
All three carriers can collect from our warehouse daily at 6 pm. ParcelLine and SwiftDrop offer a 12-month contract; Meridian requires 24 months. SwiftDrop and Meridian have both handled our peak-season volumes for other retailers of similar size, while ParcelLine's references were mainly from fashion retailers with lighter parcels.

All three carriers integrate with our warehouse management system through standard interfaces, and none would require changes to our packing process or labelling. Each offers recipients a delivery-preference service to nominate a safe place or a neighbour, and each provides proof-of-delivery photographs, which our customer service team has found useful in resolving disputes.

7. Recommendation
ParcelLine offers the lowest delivery cost, met our service requirements in the trial and reduces customer contacts through its tracking app. We recommend awarding the standard parcel contract to ParcelLine for 12 months from 1 October 2026, saving up to £76,000 a year against the alternatives.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [misread_evidence] at: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers during the trial" -- Table 1 shows ParcelLine's on-time delivery was 93.1%, below the 95% requirement. The claim (and the recommendation that ParcelLine 'met our service requirements') misreads the table; ParcelLine's 0.9% damage rate also fails the stated 0.5% requirement.
2. [unsupported_causal] at: "ParcelLine's live-tracking app clearly reduces customer contacts" -- The document states that from 1 May ParcelLine parcels alone also carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That concurrent intervention confounds the comparison, so the lower contact rate cannot be attributed to ParcelLine's tracking app.
3. [missing_consideration] at: "ParcelLine is therefore the cheapest option, saving £2,940 a month against SwiftDrop" -- The cost comparison ignores the stated £48 cost of each damaged or lost parcel. ParcelLine's damage and loss rates (0.9% and 8 per 10,000) versus SwiftDrop's (0.4% and 3 per 10,000) imply about 231 extra problem parcels a month (about £11,100), far exceeding the £2,940 price saving; ParcelLine is likely the most expensive option overall.

REVIEW:
The paper recommends ParcelLine for a 12-month contract. Its case is that ParcelLine is the cheapest on price, met the service requirements in a randomised two-month trial, and generates fewer "where is my order?" contacts.

The trial design is good, and the price arithmetic is correct. But the paper's own trial table shows ParcelLine **failed two of the four stated requirements**. Once damage and loss costs are included, ParcelLine is also the **most expensive** option, not the cheapest.

## 1. ParcelLine did not meet the requirements

Section 2 sets requirements of at least 95% on-time delivery and a damage rate below 0.5%. Table 1 shows:

| Carrier | On-time (≥95%) | Damage (<0.5%) |
|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | 96.2% ✓ | 0.4% ✓ |
| **ParcelLine** | **93.1% ✗** | **0.9% ✗** |
| Meridian | 97.5% ✓ | 0.3% ✓ |

Two statements in the paper are therefore wrong:
- Section 3: "On-time delivery was above 95% for all three carriers."
- Section 7: ParcelLine "met our service requirements in the trial."

With about 5,000 parcels per carrier, the on-time and damage gaps are large enough that chance is an unlikely explanation. The lost-parcel figures are a different matter: 8 against 3 per 10,000 means only a handful of parcels in the trial, so those numbers are too small to compare reliably.

## 2. Once damage and loss are counted, ParcelLine costs the most

Section 2 puts the cost of each damaged or lost parcel at £48, but Section 4 compares prices only. Adding damage and loss at trial rates on 42,000 parcels a month:

| Carrier | Delivery cost | Damaged + lost parcels | Cost at £48 | **Total per month** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SwiftDrop | £149,100 | ~181 | ~£8,670 | **~£157,770** |
| ParcelLine | £146,160 | ~412 | ~£19,760 | **~£165,920** |
| Meridian | £152,460 | ~134 | ~£6,450 | **~£158,910** |

Even after crediting ParcelLine's full £670 a month customer-contact saving, it costs about **£7,500 a month, or roughly £90,000 a year, more than SwiftDrop**. Damaged items are also the most common cause of one-star reviews, a cost these figures don't capture.

## 3. The drop in customer contacts can't be credited to the tracking app

Section 5 notes that from 1 May, halfway through the trial, only ParcelLine's parcels carried the new proactive delivery-day text message. That alone could explain why ParcelLine had fewer "where is my order?" contacts. It is the most likely explanation, given that ParcelLine was late *more* often than the other two carriers.

The text is also being rolled out to every carrier, so any advantage it gave ParcelLine will disappear. The £670 saving shouldn't count in ParcelLine's favour. Comparing April contacts alone, before the text began, would show whether ParcelLine had any advantage of its own.

## 4. Other risks

- **Peak season.** The contract starts in October, just before peak. ParcelLine's references are mainly fashion retailers with lighter parcels, while 30% of your parcels are 2–10 kg (lamps, mirrors, furniture). The trial ran in April and May, outside peak.
- **Off-peak trial.** All three carriers' performance in the trial may flatter how they'll do at peak. That uncertainty is largest for the carrier without comparable peak experience.

## What holds

- **The trial design.** Random allocation by the warehouse system, around 5,000 parcels each, and measures of on-time delivery, damage and loss give a fair head-to-head. Only the text-message test broke that fairness.
- **The price arithmetic.** The weighted costs of £3.55, £3.48 and £3.63, the monthly totals and the £35,000–£76,000 range are all correct.
- **The other considerations** in Section 6, such as collection times, integration and proof-of-delivery photos, are reasonable and don't separate the carriers.

## On the author's description

- **"All three carriers cleared our 95% on-time threshold."** ParcelLine recorded 93.1%.
- **"Saving between about £35,000 and £76,000 a year."** That is true of delivery prices alone. Including damage and loss, ParcelLine costs about £90,000 a year more than SwiftDrop.
- **"Shows the value of its live-tracking app."** The proactive text, which only ParcelLine had, is the likelier cause.
- **"Without compromising the customer experience."** ParcelLine had the most late, damaged and lost parcels of the three.

## What the data point to

- **SwiftDrop** is the cheapest once damage and loss are included. It meets all four requirements, offers the same 12-month term as ParcelLine, and has handled peak volumes for retailers of similar size.
- **Meridian** has the best service on every measure, at about £1,000 a month more than SwiftDrop. It requires a 24-month contract.

The choice between them is about whether Meridian's better reliability is worth roughly £13,000 a year and a longer commitment. ParcelLine should not be recommended on this evidence. The paper needs a corrected service section and a cost comparison that includes damage and loss before it goes forward.
